This being my first entry in the Fallout  series, I thought the game was decent for what it is. I've played mainly TESV: Skyrim from Bethesda Game Studios and absolutely loved it. However, lets get a couple of things clear:
1) Bethesda Game Studios Q&A is a joke. The community that surrounds these games have had to go in with the creation kit and fix a majority of the bugs and glitches in the game. Any other developer would catch a bunch of flak for this, but with BGS, its just a given.
2)The community (including modders) are what allow the game to stay relevant for years on end. The only reason games like Fallout New Vegas, Fallout 4, and Skyrim are still talked about and played has to do with the ability to mod and customize the games.
Now, with the implentation of the Creation Club, what started as a means for mod authors to be recognized for the work they have done and receive compensation for it has turned into an avenue for the empty suits to profit for a game that they've already received the asking price for. The content on CC is subpar with what is available on other mod hosting websites and even on
. Bethesda Softworks has retroactively added in microtransactions and have willingly engaged in shady business practices that the gaming community at large are against. You aren't allowed to directly purchase the items you want, you instead are forced to purchase a virtual currency, which are sold in tiered packages. Then they price the most engaging pieces of content on CC (DOOM armor and BFG) just outside what you would receive from one package, forcing you to purchase the next one up and essentially give Bethesda Softworks more money.
They won't call this paid mods (even though thats what it is) and stated they are more like mini-DLCs. Then those that have the season pass ask if they will receive this, and are told no. Guess why? They aren't DLC's. This type of corporate double talk can only come from people motivated purely by profit. This is just semantics. The content that has been offered on the Creation Club are the same things you would find on mod hosting website such as the Nexus, and those mods are of higher quality, greater variety, and FREE!
Bethesda Softworks created a wonderful game in Fallout 4. I've put hundreds of hours into the game and loved every minute of it. However, with the implementation of the Creation Club and the willingness by Bethesda to engage in shady microtransactions, going out of their way to nickel and dime the customer and reach the levels of EA, Activision, and now 2K Studios, I can't rate this game above a 4 out of 10. Ah, despair, one of those games that have been coming out dime a dozen recently. It's no wonder why horror's having a hard time nowadays.
Alright, where do I begin? First of all, I gotta say, the other reviews are right. The scariest part about this game is the "To be continued" part. Please, don't.
But I gotta say, I found it hilarious when in the main menu, instead of saying "New game" or "Play", it said "Despair"....Foreshadowing, eh?
So, you are supposed to find out what happened....What happened about what? You don't even get an explanation about why you are in that train in the first place, and you don't even get a cutscene or anything. Just a sobbing girl at first. And bam, you wake up in the middle of nowhere, in a train.
If this game is advertised as an "horror game", that's pretty much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I never got scared, or even startled, and to be fair, at least this game didn't had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ out of nowhere jumpscares like other "Pewdiepie bait" games. Which is...Somewhat of a plus, except that I didn't got to laugh at how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ they are.
Alright, I got kinda sidetracked. Despair is a generic, mediocre "Move from point A to point B" game made on the Unity engine, which means that it's got eye straining flashlight effects, of course. "Find out what happened.", that's your objective, and the only kind of explanation that the game throws at you. Alright, you start walking down a tunnel, it's dark, dark as a ♥♥♥♥ing demon's heart. Again, you move from point A from point B, waiting for something to pop out to scare you, but nothing like that happens, just the ocassional crates falling down or random loud noises.
Also, there are plenty of graphical flaws, like I can see through walls at times, and I can see what's beyond that. Also, I got bugged once, I jumped inside of a restroom stall and got trapped in there, because the game wasn't programmed to let you open that door. I had to restart the game, move at a snail's pace AGAIN through the boring♥♥♥♥♥map, and then, I managed to avoid the stalls. Turns out, I could see why you couldn't open the stall doors....They were supposed to be part of a SPOOPY jumpscare. Of course.
This game isn't even fully translated, and for a game with so much text like this one, I feel sorry for them. (Not)
For example, the notes are translated, but...I guess...Batteries? Isn't. So you have something vaguely russian sounding and "2".
There are no save points either, so if you do something dumb like me, it's back to the beggining of the game my friend. Oh, btw, the game is rather short, so that shouldn't be a problem, right? It wouldn't be a problem if you could, you know, move faster.
There comes a point where you face the, uh, I guess the main antagonist of this game, and you are chased by said antagonist, but of course, you can't control your character, he runs away on his own, and the only kind of interaction you get on that cutscene are quick time events, which shouldn't even be called quick time events because you've got a HUGE window of opportunity.
SPOILERS
The main antagonist is a girl with an axe. BAM! HORROR GOLD RIGHT THERE!
If this game was bad, I would have more to say, but it's just so mediocre that it feels like a ♥♥♥♥ing punishment to go through it.  Definitely not recommended. Don't waste your 30 minutes or so getting through this game. Don't waste those cents, neither.

In short: Looks like a 10 but plays like a 7. It doesn't set out to innovate in the genre but to pay homage to the original. Sadly the game has been abandonned by the developers so only buy if you're a MOO fan (thus the recommendation), otherwise look elsewhere.
If you're a fan of micromanaging massive empires with extreme depth and games that last many days, then look elswhere. This game is a 4/10 in terms of difficulty compared to others in the genre. But if you like being able to jump into a game with an easy learning curve and knocking a game out over a night or two, then take a look at MOO:CTS.
Side note: I've put 1113 hours into Civilization V and loved it, but dropped plaving Civ VI completely to play this instead. I'll put most of that that down to MOO:CTS looking gorgeous and also delivering just enough gameplay to satisfy versus Civ VI throwing too many options at me at once and looking like a kids cartoon. MOO:CTS reminds me of Civ V at release, incomplete but you could sense there was a great game there that with patches and DLC evolved over time into something special.
For Master of Orion series fans, here's where I'm coming from: The original MOO is one of my favourite games of all time, along with Panzer General and X-Com: Enemy Unknown. I did not like MOO2 or 3. I prefered the original due to the ease of gameplay, and while that game was probably only an objective 7, it was a 10 for what I like in a game. Easy to use, fun to play, just enough depth to keep it interesting. MOO:CTS respects the heritage of the original. Don't come into this one hoping for the depth and micromanagement of the sequels. It just doesn't have it. If, though, you liked the original but games like Stellaris seem a little too time consuming with too much of a learning curve for the time you have available, then I recommend this instead.
Summary: this is another 4x space game that aimed for the stars but hit the moon. It's still better than the vast majority that exploded on the launch pad though and fun enough to play to warrant a look. Consult your Magic 8 Ball before buying.

I am absolutely useless at horror games. Once, someone left me on my own in a dark room to play Dead Space on his phone with headphones on. I bailed before the first monster.
So I had reservations before downloading this until I realised 3 things: I was bored, I'm a broke student and the word 'Free'. What more did I need?
The key to this game's effectiveness lies in it's atmosphere, like all good games and indeed all good scary media forms. I wouldn't call the game 'scary' per se, more 'eerie'.
The premise is simple: a man waits for his wife Serena in their holiday cabin, while trying to piece their life together in his mind. The best part (no spoilers) is where there is a shift in mood: voice tone changes, eerie music creeps up on you slowly, the tone shifts and a tactile tension settles like the dust covering all this cabin's memories. The voice acting by both leads is very laudible for an independent, largely  fan-funded game.
The short version: Wonderfully atmospheric, disturbing, well-written game which will leave you uncomfortable in the best way.

Blades of Time is a classic slasher game similar to Prince of Persia series in many ways, utilizing but not coping mostly all of its features - intriguing plotline, acrobatic tricks, dynamic battles with lots of unique enemies, possibility to reverse time to solve puzzles or to defeat mob hoards and tough bosses.
Game has quite predictable but decent storyline, beautiful locations and good overall graphics as well as proper animations for characters and ambient, lots of gameplay features, such as combos, guns and magic, simple RPG elements with possibility to use different gear with unique properties, long enough campaign and interesting ‘Outbreak mode’ featuring dota-like gameplay but in the third person mode.
Fighting system much easier to learn and use then in other games, you don’t really need to focus on combos and ‘perfect’ attacks, missing few hits wont make current battle much harder or even impassable, but that doesn’t mean you can simply click whole game away. Each enemy need own strategy to deal with and bosses usually requires active usage of time rewind, temporal clones and lots of shooting, especially on hard difficulty.
Of cause Blades of Time fighting system not that advanced like in Castlevania or DMC but as for me its still much more enjoyable because it wont enrage you or cheaply delay progress every time you meet harder enemies. Moreover, local magic skills may be used nearly every second without boring grind of energy\mana like in other games, thus making whole gameplay colorful and entertaining when you really enjoy slicing’n’dicing enemies differently.
That’s why its quite weird to read negative reviews on game blaming its softcore battle system or non-AAA storyline. Just compare pricetags for Blades of Time and Castlevania for example (10€ and 30€ respectively) and titles itself after what ask yourself what did you expected to get for such a small price and from a game company for whom it was basically a debut RPG game.
The only real cons of this game is a quite dead multiplayer (still its easy to find people to play with or against via Steam community groups) and no possibility to cooperatively play story campaign, only team-up in Outbreak Mode. Quite sad because its clear that campaign levels and story itself ready to be played in coop mode, maybe game budget was too low or developers just preferred to focus on singleplayer.
Still, for a story driven game for just 10€\$ multiplayer looks more like a bonus then a mandatory feature. Thats why Im thumbing up Blade of Times and recommend this game to everybody who like hack’n’slash genre.

I was hesitant at first to buy Mad Games Tycoon until it was 50% off, but after 10+ hours of the game, I am becoming increasingly happy with the game and the community are very nice people. You, the reader already knows that you are your own game development company, but more of a Sims effect is placed in the game, because you the owner are to create different rooms including development, research, etc. and place objects in there including desks, etc. The more starred things you purchase, the better employees you hire and the further efficient your staff and you are.
Making the games is a fun process. It varies each game you produce, but it can get annoying considering it gives you hints as to whether which side you should make your game. For example, do you choose more of a focus on graphics over gameplay or vice versa, and after creating a game for that genre, it would give a suggestion to go to say, the graphics side of things. It can get very easy and with the limited amounts of genres and topics, it is easy to reproduce the same type of game with the same focus under a different name and get a high rating.
The game however, is in early access still (I'd say mid Alpha as there aren't all features implemented yet) and for right now, the basics are there, they just have to be developed more. For example, I'd love to have more of a intertwine between the games you make and how that affects the NPC world, does it affect the sales of your competitors, or vice versa. The similarities are there with Game Dev Tycoon, but I think both are distinct. They follow the same basic guideline of making games, but both do so in a different way and I personally think Mad Games Tycoon is much more in-depth so far than Game Dev Tycoon, especially in the Alpha stage.
The later part of the game (Past 2010) is not fully developed yet. The NPC companies work still the same, but I find an unbalanced effect happening. Playing in easy, by 2010, I have released about 10 games with three hitting first on the all-time charts, by 3x what the NPC game was. My three would final sell at 13+ million copies while the highest NPC one would be 4.5 million. Another example is, less features pop-up following 2010 and I have noticed by 2020, the game has stopped releasing consles, features to develop, but NPCs still release there games. To expand on this though, I'd think that everything hasn't been implemented purely because with all features so far in the game being researched, there is 41 or 42 features (and with the improvements in features like parallex scrolling compared to basic scrolling) the usable count in a AAA game (mind you, AAA games allow 50 features max) is about 33. Thats my own real flaws as it can become increasingly easy late game, but then again, I'm playing on easy and haven't really tested the higher difficulties as I had did a full playthrough of normal, but that was prior to a patch recently while buffed the difficulties of all levels.
At the moment, I'd say buy the game. I have had two full run throughs in about 10 hours, with the game setting on easy and me fast forwarding everything. It isn't a full finished product yet and the updates are regular (actually the updates coming every week or week and a half and if a hotfix is needed, a hot fix comes about 2-3 days following), though in saying that it is solid enough to have run throughs without being bored. The use of NPCs which are a major hit, different variaties of producing the game including motion capture studio, etc. and the building effect make this game a solid outing thus far, more in-depth than GDT personally, and with a suggestion thread that the developer usually follows apart from his own wishlist (though the thread will stop recieving suggestions on April 30th), the game will improve along the way and become better.
Currently, a rating is not needed but I recommend buying it at your own risk. For the average player that plays this, you can easily get 15 hours out of the game minimum, and I haven't done that yet because I had only bought it a week ago, though I have only had playthroughs mainly on easy, and will go to the next difficulty soon. If you are still hesitant following my review, if you do like these types of game, wait until it goes on sale because if it does on the summer sale, it will most likely be 50% off and will be $7.50, though sale or no sale, I think it is a must buy for the management fan.

Like many reviewers here, I saw this game first as a palate cleanser on LoadingReadyRun's Watch and Play, and bought the game during the stream. I have to say that it is well worth the £2.79, and indeed that I'd consider paying up to £6 for the provided experience. Atomic 79 is a fantastic Devil Daggers-esque arena runner where you follow your trusty mining robot (adorably designated F.R.A.N.D) around a dark crater to collect the gold it digs up, all the while avoiding and shooting the nefarious "Skeltins" that one-hit kill you if they reach your position.
Though seemingly simplistic, the game has a lot of well-designed hidden depth that enriches the experience. Gold pickups' point value is incremented based on how much gold you are already carrying without depositing it, meaning the more gold you're willing to risk, the more you get. Strong, fast enemies spawn if the regular enemy spawn limit is reached, punishing the player for playing defensively and merely avoiding the Skeltins. The player's secondary weapon (a grenade) recharges its use based on enemies killed since it was last used, rewarding aggressive play again. All the weapons (including the grenade) can be upgraded with gold collected, and helpful posters around the starting area appear as features are encountered, explaining how to deal with them.
Also of note is the fantastic soundtrack by Aeronaut, which is consistently entertaining. Overall, Atomic 79 is a great game for either long or short play: a run generally takes under 5 minutes, though I find myself chaining runs together for over an hour at a time. The price is almost trivial, and great value for the received content, and I recommend everybody with an interest in roguelites, arena runners, voxel art, cute robots, neat electronic tunes, cool and well thought-out game mechanics, moon craters, and feelings of horror and impending doom as the grenade one threw illuminates the hordes of enemies ready to replace those caught in its blast check this game out.

If you like Game Dev Tycoon, you will probably like this more. It isn't the same as GDT, there's a lot more management. You build your rooms add desks, hire staff etc. You can buy or make your own game engines, with the option to sell the engine and get a percentage of the AI developers games. There is more control over the games you create - you can buy licenses to increase the appeal of the game.
Currently the game is Early Access, and will probably stay that way for a long time although the devs do dish out updates often. With that MGT has a lot of problems:
- looks like English isn't the devs native language, you can understand the messages just about though
- massive amount of annoying messages that pop up, whenever your staff complete any project or training, any new research available, when a console is going to be released, has been released is going to be taken off the market, when it has been taken off the market, when your games get taken off the market, when your engines sell, each time your game stops until you click ok (and project/training messages require 2 ok's)
- research technology isn't consistent, particularly early on. By the time you finished your research and created an engine for it at the beginning it is already obsolete, but after year ~2000 there's hardly anything new that comes out.
-theres currently no point in doing AAA games as there is only 20 different end game technologies available.
-they recently added new consoles and stuff, which doesn't do anything for you other than more annoying messages.
-Easy and normal have no challenge to them whatsoever, and there's no end game score like in GDT. If you haven't made 200 mil by 2005 you probably wanna check your pulse. Legendary mode is rediculous, although I've only had 1 good go at it. You can make games without engines and sell them for a profit so long as your staff are fully trained, you can do contracts and make engines to sell for like 5% profit at the beginning, but everything else fails. After my best go i made a few mil, made the best engine, fully trained my staff and made a AA game with everything in it and it failed and I went bankrupt. In Easy it's the opposite, no matter what you do you will still make a profit.
-when you get a larger building and fill it with stuff the game's performance drops through the floor.
To summarise, this game is worth it if you are into sim/tycoon games. The devs do update the game often, but in it's current state only die hard tycoon game fans will clock anywhere near as many hours as i have put into this game.

A good sequel of XCOM 2012. More complex game mechanic while still having the balance of action and strategy elements. The story is quite innovative as the game put the player in the opposition (rebel) side. After several hours of playing, there are several things that I'd like to comment about this game.
Things to be improved:
1. The story is still about XCOM vs alien. As a rebel, I expect that there will be war between XCOM vs human (governments). Instead we are only facing Advent as representative of government.
2. I have a feeling that the world of XCOM is start to shift towards monsters/zombies and magic theme. I like to play XCOM for its alien/futuristic technology. Having giant cyborg or well-armed monsters is ok. But introducing 'the lost' or 'warlock' in War of The Chosen is like trying to make XCOM into Resident Evil or D&D games. Dear firaxis and 2k games, please stay with the hi-tech extra terrestrially theme in the future sequel and dlc.
3. Metal support for Mac would be nice. As per graphic quality, I think graphic engine of XCOM 2012 is already enough for me. Instead of putting more effort in making better graphics, I think it is better to allocate it on story, platform optimisation (such as support for metal), new weapons/tech tree, or even new kind of relationship between XCOM and various organisation (such as found in X-COM Apocalypse). I'm referring to Star Wars KotOR 1&2. Not every sequel needs to increase the graphics requirement significantly to be better than the previous game.
And the good things are:
1. Still have interesting research-tree and a lot of things to read (if you like to really immerse your self into XCOM world).
2. Right amount of difficulty. You can start from easiest level to get your self comfortable with all the game elements, and increase difficulty later for more pleasure.
3. This game is highly replayable. Beware: You may want to never reach the final mission and always hunger for more wars.
Overall I still consider it as a good sequel of XCOM 2012. If you like alien or sci-fi themed game as I do, this one is for you.

Heroes Rise: The Hero Project is an entertaining story, and it is bigger than its predecessor, but I found it to be a weaker entry overall.
While Heroes Rise: The Prodigy deals with the protagonist starting his career as a hero and most of the choices revolve around how the hero uses their powers, Heroes Rise: The Hero Project moves the protagonist onto a super-powered reality TV show. While the writing is still fun, and I still like the characters, suddenly the story branching points are less about the actual heroing and more about the petty politics of a Survivor style reality TV show. Presumably, this story is more mutable by the player as a result, but I found the choices to be less exciting.
Ultimately, I would still recommend this title because it is an entertaining super-powered romp with a really, really fun climax. It also gives the (presumably) upcoming third instalment a really good kick-off.

This game gets old fast. I like Hack and Slash games a lot, but this is one I don't really care for. It feels like there's almost no impact to the combat in the game and some of the enemies are pretty cheap. You can die pretty fast if you don't look at your health bar because your character doesn't react to most damage at all and there's no block button which is sorely needed. All you can do for defense is either run away or attack and hope to stun lock the enemies with your swords, but there are certain enemies that only take damage from your special attacks. This leads to boss fights where you have to build up rage for the special attacks by beating up smaller enemies and the boss just spams attacks at you that you can't block. It could have been alright if they'd added a few things, but as it stands it's just kind of frustrating.
I can't really recommend this. Even though I only spent $2 on this, I feel like it was kind of a waste. Stilted ialogue, combat not fleshed out enough, and a story that's very much in the background make me regret buying it.  If you want a hack and slash game with fanservice in it, just get Senran Kagura or something.

- отриц. частица, и
- смотреть). 1) слепота. 2) в переносном значении: тупоумие, потеря умственных способностей".
Игра Ablepsia, разработанная NedoStudio, повествует о слепом старце, обладающем весьма необычной способностью. В его власти одним прикосновением заставлять уличные фонари, погасшие в результате неизвестного события,  снова светить.  От игрока требуется помочь этому экстраординарному электромонтеру  вернуть освещение в шести локациях, устраняя различные опасности, возникающие на его пути. Зажав клавишу Пробел на клав-е, можно остановить фигурку персонажа, с помощью ЛКМ накрыть крышкой открытый  колодезный люк или потушить костер. По нажатию Shift старичок будет семенить с удвоенной скоростью. Вот все возможности, к-рые  способен дать игровой процесс.
Назову  недостатки:
• Скудное музыкальное сопровождение.
• Однообразность происходящего быстро вызывает скуку.

This game has a LOT of bugs. Driving through intersections your car reacts like it hit something. Your cursor can randomly get stuck. The ballistics make no sense, e.g. shooting at a vehicle window and nothing is happening.
Gameplay is clunky, largely because of the horrible driving mechanics. Other commentors have said the driving is like Crazy Taxi; that is wholly accurate. There are some good parts of the game, but overall the game is repetitive and the flow of gameplay is hampered by the whole "stress" situation. This game would benefit a lot from a campaign, or at least set missions like in GTA. You need a car when off duty, but you only make like $500 a shift and your net income is more like $100 a shift after vehicle repairs (necessary due to aforementioned clunky driving and the fact that ramming cars is the only way to stop vehicles that do not pull over). The cheapest car is like $16,000. You can call taxis...but not to your house.
So far I've been exploiting the bugs in the game to actually get any play in. For example, I quit after going off duty and then when I log back in I'm in my house, fully rested and fed. I also call my sister, who apparently drops me back at my house after we're done hanging out.
There are so many elements of this game that just feel very amateurish and silly. I do not recommend this. Get LCPDFR, a mod for GTA IV.

First I would like to say that I only have over 100 hours on this game, but I have been in the community since the first week it came out on steam with a few of my friends. If you just want to read if people should get the game look at the “final statement:” paragraph. If you want to know how the game was or my opinion, read the rest of the super long review. (you might enjoy it)
Summary of the game: when my friends and I first started, everything was priced in Cubits. And I mean EVERYTHING from new classes, to new mounts, to anything in the market EXCEPT the costumes. Was there patron back then, yes but there was no reason for paying. If I remember, shadow level was the highest tier people could get but don’t quote me. It was great that a person could get shadow level gear and get to Uber-3, buy a class coin, rinse and repeat. The guys and I were picking which was the best class for the three of us. Back then shadow portals was the only raid portal and sky was for the top players. I stopped playing for a while and came back and what a change that was. The shadow grade gear was mediocre, there was so much more in game, and the market was majority patron points. It was like a completely different game. Now there is lunar and eclipse tiers in the shadow portal, Uber-9 level portals and sublevels so people can get different items in different biomes.
My reaction: So much new stuff but none of it is meant for the beginner class person, it feels like. It starts with a person who gets to pick a class and hopes to God that they pick the right one. If the person didn’t they would have to either grind to get a class token from mastering point or use real money to buy a class coin. Then they would grind and shoot through the beginning levels which is the way it was in the beginning. but after Uber-2, it feels like you hit a wall and people would have to grind and grind to get a higher power rank. The portals don’t even use the level system anymore; it is power rank from the person’s gear that they go to a higher portal. if a person is a free to play (f2p) person the market is basically useless. Everything there is bought from patron points.
One thing to fix the game and make it better: Now I know there is no such thing as perfection but having this fixed would make the game the next best thing. Let the market be the way as it was in the beginning. Have it to where anyone can get the items using Cubits. The producers can also have it to where people can use patron points to get the items faster and that would be fine as well. Getting what the people need and getting a few bucks on the side is great. Or at least make the class coin purchasable with Cubits.
Final opinion: So, the question is,” is the game good for people to play?” I would say yes but the game is more fun if you play with friends in a group. The multiplayer buff (a buff to where multiple players would get the same XP or resource from a one item) is totally worth it. The game rewards people if they work together which is good and it should.  If you don’t like the game, what did you lose. It is a free game.

I love this game; it's by far my favorite. I want to tackle what people often dislike about the game first in my review. People typically believe this game is pay to win, it's very grindy, and get's repetitive after awhile. I've been playing for a year and can contest to all of these. As any game is nowadays, you can pay and get further ahead in the game. This doesn't automatically make this pay to play. I've spent months free to play and pay to play. Either way is extremely fun for me because the game itself is still the same. The grinding aspect is somewhat true if you want to level up and get strong. I don't believe this to be a problem though because it's not meant to be a game that you can progress in rapidly, paying or not paying. I've completed several thousands of dungeons and I will continue doing so, because it's enjoyable to me. As for the repitition of doing things in the game, I disagree with completely. If you play this game for maybe a week I can maybe understand getting lost or confused as to how some things work. This often offputs people from playing but I highly suggest communicating with other players, especially higher levels, to figure out how to do things. Do not beg because nobody wants to help someone who begs.
Pros:
- Not pay to win/play
- Plenty of stuff to do :building your own "house" you can take anywhere or building in a club of your own, whatever you want, collecting items for mastery, doing casual tasks such as fishing, mining ore, or using the marketplace to buy and sell goods, etc!
- Constantly new items being added and events happening
- Streams of developers talking about new updates frequently
- Lots of different classes to choose from and play, all with different abilities
- Tons more pros...
Cons:
- There are bugs that still exist, but do not take away from the big picture that is the game.
- Lag is a problem that exists for majority of players, mainly because of the servers. If there are many people in a world, it will lag more.
- They created new hourly challenges that are difficult to complete with how bad the lag is sometimes.
- Critique and advice given from players to developers aren't always heard
In no way do I suggest not trying this game out. The more time you put into it, the more you'll fall in love. It's not perfect, but what game is?

GMT was a shining gem of a server in the golden days of Garry's Mod, and Tower Unite is its continuation in every sense of the word. Tower Unite aims to replicate the old GMod Tower experience as closely as possible, using a different engine and, of course, as a standalone game.
To that end, Tower Unite is clearly still a work in progress. The optimization and netcode need some fine-tuning, and it doesn't have all of the amenities GMT had before its end, but that is explicitly only a temporary downside, as the developers are hard at work improving and updating their game.
In the end, if you're very interested in recalling the old GMT experience, Tower Unite will scratch nearly all your itches. Don't go in expecting a complete experience, but don't also go in expecting a dead game.

This is an amazing little arena shooter.
So, you're a person with a robot in a cursed crater in space. Possibly on the moon? The gravity is low, so the controls take some getting used to. I don't think they're bad, they just make your character feel like you have momentum.
Your robot is mining gold from the crater for you, and your job is to get the gold back to your base, while defending yourself from an onslaught of skeltins, skells and worse. There's a really clever greed mechanic that gives you more gold for waiting longer to deposit in in the bank, with the obvious penalty of losing everything you're carrying if you die. It's absolutely gotten me several times, but it's just so tempting ...
Anyway, it's difficult, but with the persistent upgrade system, you feel like you're actually progressing. I don't know what the endgame is, the longest I've been able to live is just over 3 minutes. I know I'm going to have fun finding out.
So, other things.
This game feels like it's tuned to make you grin, even while it's kicking your teeth down your throat. From the little informational posters in your base//office to the voxel-cute enemies  (except the bone balls. those things are freaky) the whole thing feels like it's got an great sense of humor.
The sound design is solid, and the music is very good. (OST DLC PLS?) I think it might get repetitive at some point, but I haven't lived long enough for that yet.

DayZ is a mod for Arma 2 that turns the base game into a zombie survival simulator. DayZ is one of the most detailed, if not the most detailed, and immersive zombie survival sims available. When you play DayZ, you create a character and spawn on a beach with nothing but your clothes and from there you have to make your way inland and try to find the tools you need to fend off the undead and to survive in this new world. Generally you are looking for things such as a melee weapon, medical supplies, light sources, food and you might even be lucky enough to find a gun or camping gear.
As you make your way through formerly populated areas like villages, farms and the three large cities, you will run into hordes of zombies that you will have to deal with. You can lose them by running into buildings or otherwise breaking line of sight with them. But the zombies are actually not the real threat in this game; the biggest potential threat comes from the other players who are attempting to survive just like you. Some of them will try to help you or trade with you, but usually in exchange for something of equal value, or if you are both being attacked by zombies or other players and you band together out of desperation. Most players though, are bandits, which you can tell by their clothes and covered faces. These players are out for your blood, and only want the stuff they can loot off your dead body.
You want to be very cautious in approaching other survivors that you do not know in DayZ because a lot of bandit groups will try to bait victims by having one of their number pose as a "friendly" and then when the victim runs over to trade or help, the rest of the bandits ambush him or her. Players in this game have gotten very paranoid in the last year and a half, and so a lot of times players will shoot each other on sight rather than risk losing their gear to a potential bandit.
So what do you actually do in DayZ once you have your basic weapons and tools needed to survive? Well you want to find a safe place that you can use as a home base. Generally you want to be far away from areas frequented by zombies, so somewhere in the woods usually. You want to be close enough to a town that you can raid it for supplies every few hours but far enough that zombies and players will have a difficult time tracking you home.
Once you have your things safely stashed, the best thing you can do is band together with your friends or any friendly people on the server you can find and get a vehicle. A bicycle is great for solo scout and loot missions to town, but a car, truck or SUV will provide cover from bullets, a large inventory and quick transport for multiple people. Focus on getting the necessary car parts you will need to fix up one of the junked cars you find laying around. After that, once you get enough loot and establish a territory, you can even build a house in some versions of DayZ and barricade it against zeds and meddlesome players.
At some point you will get into a fight with another player. Most of the time these fights aren't fair. Maybe a group of players rolled up on you while you were looting and shot you as you came out of a house. Other times you'll follow someone and not realize that they have friends with them and their friends flank and kill you, or you just get shot by someone while you are running from zombies that have aggroed you. All of these things will happen to you on a regular basis, and since everything stays on your corpse when you die, chances are they will loot and take your stuff. But other times you get lucky and you kill a guy with a huge gun that you need because you were lucky enough to catch him with his pants down. So now you have a big gun, and then when you go around the side of the house he was in, you find his giant military truck full of more guns and supplies. Now you are a zombie slaying god and you can bring all of that back to your base.
It is very easy to either get very, very mad at this game and ragequit or try to keep deaths in perspective, play smart and take all the opportunities you get. If you are observant and patient in every situation you will do well. If you run into a building without checking the surroundings for players watching or for zombies that will attract attention to you, you will die a lot. If you take your time and all necessary precautions you will catch somebody making a mistake and profit from it, and continue to survive the apocalypse.

A good sequel of XCOM 2012. More complex game mechanic while still having the balance of action and strategy elements. The story is quite innovative as the game put the player in the opposition (rebel) side. After several hours of playing, there are several things that I'd like to comment about this game.
Things to be improved:
1. The story is still about XCOM vs alien. As a rebel, I expect that there will be war between XCOM vs human (governments). Instead we are only facing Advent as representative of government.
2. I have a feeling that the world of XCOM is start to shift towards monsters/zombies and magic theme. I like to play XCOM for its alien/futuristic technology. Having giant cyborg or well-armed monsters is ok. But introducing 'the lost' or 'warlock' in War of The Chosen is like trying to make XCOM into Resident Evil or D&D games. Dear firaxis and 2k games, please stay with the hi-tech extra terrestrially theme in the future sequel and dlc.
3. Metal support for Mac would be nice. As per graphic quality, I think graphic engine of XCOM 2012 is already enough for me. Instead of putting more effort in making better graphics, I think it is better to allocate it on story, platform optimisation (such as support for metal), new weapons/tech tree, or even new kind of relationship between XCOM and various organisation (such as found in X-COM Apocalypse). I'm referring to Star Wars KotOR 1&2. Not every sequel needs to increase the graphics requirement significantly to be better than the previous game.
And the good things are:
1. Still have interesting research-tree and a lot of things to read (if you like to really immerse your self into XCOM world).
2. Right amount of difficulty. You can start from easiest level to get your self comfortable with all the game elements, and increase difficulty later for more pleasure.
3. This game is highly replayable. Beware: You may want to never reach the final mission and always hunger for more wars.
Overall I still consider it as a good sequel of XCOM 2012. If you like alien or sci-fi themed game as I do, this one is for you.

After plopping down $3.99 for the Heroes Rise Bundle, I can honestly say that it was one of the better spent $4.00 in my entire life.
I've since played through the interactive novel (better description than game) at least 3 times exploring various aspects of the game.
One really caused me to write this review, however, was how engaging the novel was. It is extremely well written, with complex characters (some aspects chosen by you the player, in how NPC's are described) and motivations which affect how the story goes into the sequel as well. I actually became quite attached to my character, and replayed the game if I ever made a gaffe I didn't like. (Sometimes I was cursing myself for making silly mistakes, other times I wanted to explore various choices and see there effects).
Two issues I have to disagree with in a small critique. Choices concerning saving lives or taking them ought to trump any ideology your character pursues.  There are instances in the game where your choices are locked into one decision or another based on previous choices your character has made. I disagree with this aspect, and hope the author will fix such issues to open the life/death choices in the novel to either choice regardless of chosen path.
The 2nd issue involves the first, and I'm not quite sure if this is a bug, since I was unable to save game at midpoints. I suppose saving games midstory would detract from the choices one, but it really would be nice if that feature were available, so that I wouldn't have to restart each game from scratch to explore various choices.
Otherwise, I really enjoyed the series, and again, for $4.00 got a lot of hours of gameplay in. Seeing as I usually rate games based upon how much the cost per hour I play, I'd say this interactive novel is easily a 10/10.

I totally did not play this for the easy 100% achievements.
Oh wait, yes I did. Because that it the only way I could have tolerated this abysmal game for more than 90 seconds.
I received Ablepsia in a bundle, and registered it because I thought, "seriously, how bad can it be?" Well, really, really bad. Like Michael Jackson's "Bad" bad. Like Huey Lewis' "Sometimes Bad is Bad" bad. Just bad all around.
The controls are horrendous, leaving your left hand stretched across the space bar and shift key while your right hand works the mouse. The keys are not remappable. Clicking or tapping on objects is inaccurate while the screen scrolls. Your hands hate you during every second of gameplay.
And speaking of gameplay...well, there practically is none. Nothing really changes throughout the game -- you just get more obstacles to clear as you go up levels. But the strategy to win is simply to stop your blind guy with the space bar, clear everythig on the screen, walk up close to the next set of spikes, stay put until your boost is full, sprint past the spikes...and rinse and repeat to the end of the level. The person that greets you at the end of each level (city) says the exact same thing every time. It's a yawnfest from beginning to end.
There is nothing graphically that makes one city different than another (other than some snow on the very last level), nor anything visually interesting going on, well, ever.
What's sad is that there is a kernel of an interesting concept here: a blind guy as a hero who, in a world of darkness, essentially has super powers. Just think of all of the cool things that the devs could have done here -- but didn't.
I can't blame them for a card-based cash grab, since the game doesn't drop any cards. But even at less than a buck in US dollars, I can't imagine anyone ever paying money for this thing. I wrote more interesting games in BASIC in the 80s as a little kid.
Long story short, you should avoid this game. The only reason you should register and play it is if you get it in a bundle and decide to tolerate playing this thing for 30 minutes to get the easy 100% completion and add up a few more easy cheevos.

Avoid this game. There are problems before you even start the actual game. When you boot up the game, there is no mouse cursor and the arrow keys don't work. Only through trial and error was I able to figure out that you had to use the A & D keys to move the arrow. But when you try to hit the enter key, it does absolutely nothing. Instead, you have to press the mouse button.
In the config menu, there is no way to change the key settings so you are stuck with what they give you. You can lower the volume but it tricks you into thinking that you actually had control of the volume. If you wait a minute on the config screen, the volume magically goes back up to full. Even if you lower the volume to silent, once you start the game, there is sound.
Now onto the actual gameplay, if you can even call it that. This is a top down shooter that is trying to look like the games of old. But the graphics are ugly and the backgrounds are distracting, making it hard to see what is happening on screen. The point is to rescue all the people within the given time limit. There are enemies and you have a gun on your vehicle but it all seems unnecessary. The enemies don't do enough damage to even bother shooting them. Gameplay basically boils down to a maze-like runner, hoping to find all the people before time runs out.
If you paid for this game, you should demand a refund. The only redeeming thing that it has going for it is that it has steam trading cards. Just let this game run in the background for a hour and collect your free cards. Remember to turn off your speakers or unplug your headphones because there will be sound, no matter how hard you try.

I love this game; it's by far my favorite. I want to tackle what people often dislike about the game first in my review. People typically believe this game is pay to win, it's very grindy, and get's repetitive after awhile. I've been playing for a year and can contest to all of these. As any game is nowadays, you can pay and get further ahead in the game. This doesn't automatically make this pay to play. I've spent months free to play and pay to play. Either way is extremely fun for me because the game itself is still the same. The grinding aspect is somewhat true if you want to level up and get strong. I don't believe this to be a problem though because it's not meant to be a game that you can progress in rapidly, paying or not paying. I've completed several thousands of dungeons and I will continue doing so, because it's enjoyable to me. As for the repitition of doing things in the game, I disagree with completely. If you play this game for maybe a week I can maybe understand getting lost or confused as to how some things work. This often offputs people from playing but I highly suggest communicating with other players, especially higher levels, to figure out how to do things. Do not beg because nobody wants to help someone who begs.
Pros:
- Not pay to win/play
- Plenty of stuff to do :building your own "house" you can take anywhere or building in a club of your own, whatever you want, collecting items for mastery, doing casual tasks such as fishing, mining ore, or using the marketplace to buy and sell goods, etc!
- Constantly new items being added and events happening
- Streams of developers talking about new updates frequently
- Lots of different classes to choose from and play, all with different abilities
- Tons more pros...
Cons:
- There are bugs that still exist, but do not take away from the big picture that is the game.
- Lag is a problem that exists for majority of players, mainly because of the servers. If there are many people in a world, it will lag more.
- They created new hourly challenges that are difficult to complete with how bad the lag is sometimes.
- Critique and advice given from players to developers aren't always heard
In no way do I suggest not trying this game out. The more time you put into it, the more you'll fall in love. It's not perfect, but what game is?

This game has a LOT of potential. So far, in its early stages, it's proven to be a very fun game. I played it for about 2 hours and got to level 4. I was a little disappointed that I couldn't figure out how exactly I can get my new car.
Now, in the start, you have to spend the first 5 minutes just reading through a very long text that explains how everything works. Instead, I'd suggest a categorized way of looking through things. That way it's better to look over things later on as well.
The game mechanics are.. they're not the best. It's sluggish, the car handling is pretty crap and civilians driving trucks often cause traffic jams because they can't turn a tight corner. As far as civilian interaction goes and completing missions that involve finding suspects, it's pretty much impossible. I mean my first callout was a vandalism case. I asked the guy who called what the vandals look like and he gave me the descriptions of them. Problem was, the descriptions matched like 3 nearby NPCs. I'd have no way of knowing which one of them is the real criminal. Some diversity in appearances would be nice. Just retexture the clothes, if you must.
DUIs are a little confusing. So I check someones breath and they're under the influence. I get them out, place them under arrest and it gets ticked under "Innocent Civilians Arrested"? DUI is an arrestable crime in pretty much every state in America. Wut.
As far as on-duty off-duty time goes, I think there's way too much effort put into the off-duty aspect. The stress level is.. meh. Hanging out with your mother/sister/grandparents/friends doesn't even give you any stress points, which is weird. And what's with the applause as if I've just won an Oscar after hanging out with people?
The police vehicle itself is well done, as well as the interactables. Indicators, siren and the strobes themselves. However, it being just red is kind of bland. Red and blue in the future pls. Oh and while I think to mention it, please add a tutorial on how to get a new police vehicle, because I have not got a clue on how to get my new ones.
The game is built on a strange engine as well. I mean the graphics aren't really top of the line and I'm lagging horribly unless I run it under low graphics. It doesn't make much sense that I can run Payday 2 better than I can run this.
There should also be a little bit of further research be done on the ranks. I mean you don't have Police Officer and then Senior Deputy. Deputy = Sheriff's Office/Department (county). Police Officer = Police Department (city).
All in all, like I said, it's a pretty good game with a lot of potential. Needs a lot of polishing. I mean the English itself in the game is sometimes bizarre.

I've never been a fan of early access. Also, I have never written a worthwhile review before. This game changed my mind on both of those.
***How I feel about Early Access and these developers***
My problem with early access, I've seen to many games cost $20+ for a game that is anywhere from 10-40% complete, and that just doesn't seem fair to the consumer. I have also heard when games have been sold cheap for Early Access but then has to be repurchased upon realease. Both of these are reasons that kept me away from Early Access. This team of developers has changed my mind on this. Eggcode has made me happy to finally be a pleased supporter of an Early Access game. They release a sizeable update approximately every week. It shows that they care about their project even though they could take the money and run right now. Also, when I bought this it was clear and upfront that the game was considered 15% whole. This was a great change than what I've seen. With each update it shows that they are listening to the customers and are on top of things like the small details such as March 24th when to numbers would display switched with each other. This didn't need to get tackled so rapidly, but they chose to be on top of even the small details.
***The Game***
This may or may not be the most accurate depiction of the game based upon when you read it because updates are happening approximately weekly. The game had a good bell curve of difficulty. I felt like I was trying to climb and try every angle at the beginning with little success but enough to stay afloat. As you succeed at creating games or doing contract work you can afford to keep employees. They are not extremely dynamic yet, but after about 2 employees they start requiring items such as a couch for "sitting," vending machines, (humorously) toilets, arcade games, etc. These employees have monthly salaries which make you have to continue working. The employees cost more as they level up later in the game. You can train your avatar as well as your employees which lead to better games and faster contract work, but cost more as the get better.
Your employees have multiple facets: making games, contract work to make some quick money, marketing to sell more games, customer service to keep your fan base happy, and research.
The games seem to change with time. At the beginning you can make a game that sells "enough" to keep you going, but as the game progresses your one man or woman indie game team won't keep you alive. Later in the game it does take a team to make good games happen fast enough to sell on whatever the current market is.
There is more to say about this game. I spent 20+ hours making 10+ billion dollars and called it quits at that point with a team of 25 fully trained game developers, 8 customer service pros, and 8 marketing pros. I look forward to "replaying" this game as the updates progress, and hopefully I can update this review as time progresses.

Note: This is a long review so if you plan on reading read to the end
So this is a game I had picked up recently due to the interest I had had in it a while back. Playing games like this I find pretty enjoyable and  have done my fair share of Game Dev Tycoon, seeing this I immediately jumped to the conclusion that this was a rip off of that very game.
And boy was I wrong
So not only is this a game that takes the functions of Game Dev Tycoon and other Game Dev Sims it improves on it greatly allowing you to go into a deeper creation of your games, although not too far away from where it's aging older brother set the benchmark. By this I mean the ability to impliment copy protection for your games allow it to be released in other languages because it isn't all about the english speaking world and above all else it expands on what Game Dev does with it's combinations.
What does this mean? Well this is quite simple where Game Dev had the massive list of topics with the  5 root genres with the 6th researchable one of casual games coming into effect early on along with Multi-genre and MMO being unlocked later into the game, Mad Games Tycoon  goes balls to the wall with the progression of time since Game Dev's release these roots have branched off  to a collection of 16 genres for you to combine with one another to experiment and create the best games, and as time goes on maybe this will increase even more.
The Key element of this gameplay however is the other side to it, Game Dev is you sitting at your desk making money by making good games and then having you move into a bigger space and hire more people to sit at deska and help you make money, that may be putting it bluntly and to be fair there is other stuff to do like research and so on but stripped to it's core that is game dev. Mad Games Tycoon however decides to borrow elements from the late Maxis'  collosal franchise of the sims where you have to care for these people in more depth, you give people the multitude of rooms to work in along with a bathroom and break room as well as tending to their needs so their will to work for you is great this hopefully allowing you to get more done in your games and tilt the tide to get that higher rating and more money.
There is however one issue with this game that I have and that could partially be blamed on me as well. Mad Games Tycoon at the moment of me writing this review has no tutorial mode and if it does I can't find it, It does have an easy mode option which starts you off in an office space however but that really doesn't do much when it comes to learning the mechanics and the key gameplay elements. it took me a while to find out how to even build a room to work in let alone make a game and even then the sliders are easy to work around, but i wasn't too sure on how it would work. With words either side of the bar  I was unsure if moving it closer to one way meant it was a higher priority or that it meant it was a lower one because of the way Game Dev worked with the bigger bar meaning more time, and i'm honestly still not sure to this day.
Don't let this bring you down as eventually when you learn how the game works you can easily get into the game even with the difficulty. all of these games are the same fundementally with the rinse and repeat and if you don't succeed try again aproach with the idea that someday you will hit it big and from then it is smooth sailing.
Overall then this is a strong game even in it's early access state and is in strong standing within the Game Dev Games, although this review constantly made comparison to Game Dev  it does not mean I think of it as a worse game, I would honeslty say I believe that Mad Games Tycoon in it's current form is on par even without the tutorial and I really hope to see this game through to a full release where then it could take it's place on the throne of where Game Dev Tycoon currently resides

LOL FIRST PRODUCT REVIEW!... Nimble Quest review:
Nimble Quest decides to put a spin on the classic snake formula by making the snake a conga line of adventurers who have to kill conga lines of monsters. Does it work? Yes.
The game is simple enough for almost anyone to pick up and play immediately, and just challenging enough to make you want to keep playing and unlock all the various adventurers. Nimble Quest features 16 unlockable heroes to play as (your snake will only ever be at most 16 units long, no duplicate heroes.) and they all feel different which is quite nice, 4 power-ups that can be dropped by enemies and upgrades for everything. this helps flesh out the game and adds more of a reason to keep playing just to see how far in you can get. Also there is a sizeable army of monsters to fight against as well. There's also guilds that you can make to try to become the best in the world w friends but they're not that special.
All-in-all if you like snake but wanna play a game that mixes up the formula than I say go for it.

(Note: I received a copy of this game for free. I also tested it during development. My time played on Steam is not indicative of how much I actually played this game.)
Let me start by saying this is not typically a style of game I get a lot of enjoyment out of. I'm a pretty casual gamer, and as such, games that punish me are usually a huge turn-off. I tend to play them long enough to discover I suck at them, then never play them again.
That being said, I frickin
this game. It makes me mad, but in such a way that I become determined and
to play one more round. It's the perfect combination of simple gameplay and punishing difficulty. The music is catchy and keeps me amped, but doesn't overstay it's welcome. The 3D-pixel-art visual style is a nice mix of retro and modern. The setting and enemies are unique and have a weird, spooky cuteness to them. I particularly like the small range of visibility. Enemies seem to walk out of the darkness at you from every angle. Every death scares the bejeezus out of me and usually sends me into a fit of rage-laughter.
My only real complaint is that I can't seem to buy upgrades as quickly as I want to, but that is 100% attributed to my skill level. And I can sort of understand complaints about the sort of slippery-feeling controls, but after a few trips to the pit, I adjusted and no longer noticed it. It seemed appropriate to me, given that the game is set in spooky space.
I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that likes gauntlet-style games, especially shooters. While I received this game for free, I do think the price is ridiculously reasonable. It's hard to find a game this good looking and fun for less than five bucks!

Definitely a beautiful game, in storyline, the art and music, and atmosphere that it creates.
It's simple and easy to play; no puzzles, just clicking around in the environment. I don't think  scary is the exact term to describe the game, but rather dark. The surroundings give off a creepy vibe, but nothing that'll give you the heebie-jeebies (okay maybe if you're like playing at 2 in the morning with the lights off, but even then it's nothing that'll kill you).
The storyline is pretty unique. The entire game takes place in a cabin, very old, very vintage looking. Your wife is gone, and it seems to be quite some time. Throughout the game, you seek clues around the cabin in order to unravel the story behind the past years. It starts off very calm, very in-love, and nice, but as the story progresses, the mood and tone takes a completely different turn. The fate of your wife becomes clearer as it comes closer, but the actual ending of the game is very unexpected. It's a huge plot-twist, that both provokes your thoughts and pretty much leaves you speechless.
If you're not a fan of puzzles/strategy, but enjoy a gr8 storyline and creepypasta stuff, you should definitely check it out, especially since it's free.

Blades of Time is a nice 3rd person action game with some cool mechanics and it looks good to boost. The enviroments are nice and varied, the enemies less so, but fun to fight nonetheless.
Fighting is pretty standard, normal attacks, magic attacks, and even 3rd person shooting.
The most notable mechanic is time manipulation, and you can have some pretty cool fun with it, distracting enemies with shields with a clone while you sneak behind them where they're vulnerable, piling up on them with 3 of your clones shooting a minigun at one enemy, attacking them with swords on all sides. It's pretty fun. It's also used for solving puzzles. They're not exactly brain teasers, but serve a purpose to mix things up.
There are secrets to find, some items to collect, and a co-op mode that i haven't tried but that seems to be dead. Try it with a friend if you can.
Also, to my great surprise seeing as how rarely games support that, even some big name developers don't seem to grasp the concept - this game supports hybrid gamepad and mouse input. Your mouse isn't disabled if you use a gamepad. This is especially good for Steam controller users, and the game is a delight to play as a result of that because you have better precission while shooting and are not limited to analog speeds.
All in all, this is a great port, no issues whatsoever, and the devs actually understood how to program the game for a PC. It's amazing how big name studios tend to mess up ports, but a smaller studio makes a good job.
The colors are a bit washed up, i guess that's the aesthetic they were going for, i didn't care much for that, but you can fix it as you like with SweetFX easily though so no big deal.
The story starts interesting, then looses itself a bit from the middle to the end, but all in all it's ok. If you want a good story play some RPG's or something. The story here is adequate, nothing horrible, nothing impressive.
Very recommended. If you have doubts, get it on sale.

Realm of the Mad God is the first ever free to play Bullet Hell MMO. Team up with dozens of players and battle through the Realm of the Mad God, Oryx. With a retro 8-bit style, Realm is an evolution of traditional MMO gameplay. A dozen classes and hundreds of items to discover means Realm is easy to play but difficult to master. Players can jump in Realm for 5 minutes or stay online for hours because there is nothing to install or download.
Key Features
Action combat! No turn-based battles here, only skilled running and gunning.
Epic boss battles. Navigate demented waves of bullets from nasty demons.
True cooperative play. All experience is shared and you win by playing together.
Great 8-bit art: Retro styling straight from the 8-bit era.
Over a dozen unique character classes. Play as a powerful wizard, a clever mystic, a brawling warrior.
Loot! Hundreds of weapons, potions, armors, and rings.
PermaDeath. Dying well means something in Realm. Earn fame if you survive for long enough and kill enough monsters.
Sheep. The sheep say 'Baa.'

A lot of people are going to compare Mad Games Tycoon to Game Dev Tycoon, and it's understandable why. They're both tycoon games based around game development. So the question is- which is better?
That's a difficult one.
Mad Games Tycoon definitely feels like a much deeper game. Unlike Game Dev Tycoon, you can actually build your office, which is a plus. You can also have multiple teams of people working on different things, instead of everyone working on the same thing, which is a huge plus. However, the actual game making part feels a little more satisfying in Game Dev Tycoon. With Game Dev Tycoon, you have to adjust things every so often in the game making process, while in Mad Games Tycoon, you do everything at the start and you wait. Admittedly, with the ability to have multiple groups of people doing multiple things, it doesn't feel like you're just sitting around and waiting for the most part, but I've had a few moments where I got rather bored just waiting for a game to get finished.
The one big thing that Mad Games Tycoon has going for it is that features are still being added. I've had the game for a week, maybe a week and a half, and it's already seen two updates that have changed up the gameplay significantly. Game Dev Tycoon, as good as it is, is a finished game. Sure, you can add some mods to the game to keep it fresh, but what you see is what you get, and it's all you're going to get. Mad Games Tycoon, on the other hand, is still evolving, still making changes to keep the game fresh, and that's why I prefer Mad Games Tycoon to Game Dev Tycoon.
The game's not perfect by any stretch of the imagination. There are some things I wish they made a little more clear, the lack of mod support is kind of a bummer (Though, it still being in development, I can understand) and sometimes the staff gets upset by silly things, but I've plugged a bunch of time into this game and I plan to plug a bunch more into it. Definitely worth picking up.

A game with a story full of more holes and unexplained happenings than Swiss cheese, but the game and combat itself is so fun you won't care. Combat is super fluid and hyper mobile, everything cancellable into everything else, and the time rewind function allows you to fight alongside an army of your own clones that will all repeat your actions, including magic and combos, allowing for an impressive amount of screen filling VFX spamming power. There is no block button, but thats's fine, because you'r etoo busy flyig and dashing aorund and stabbing everything and blowing it up with magic.
Puzzles are minimal and generally rely on timed button pressing with the use of the time rewind mechanic. Game is 100% linear with some small collectibles that try to flesh out the happenings, but honestly, it doesn't really matter in this case. Nothing really gets explained except for one story point you can see coming from the opening scenes of the game. Story shouln't be why you play the game though - it'll be for the impressive hack and slash combat. If I had to give the game some downsides: Platforming elements are a little shaky since jump momentum is awkward, and the upgrades and loot items really aren't all that impressive,  save for the jump to level 2 spells, which is incredibly impressive.
Game has a multiplayer mode, but apparently it's dead and I didn't touch it, no clue there.

I honestly don't understand the complaints I'm seeing about the controls being "slippy." It's a physics based game, and as such you accelerate and decelerate, but they don't feel slippy to me. Like all games, it took a few runs to get a feel for it, but honestly within 5-10 minutes it felt pretty natural.
The music is top-notch, and goes through a really nice loop. A lot of times I find myself getting irritated with songs in games where you continually start over repeatedly, but so far I haven't gotten sick of it. I also really enjoy the speed at which the difficulty ramps up. It takes a minute or two to really get going, which feels like just the right amount of time to warm up and get into the flow. The art style is also super cute! It manages to be both dark and super colorful at the same time, and I love the design of the "spooky" skeletons.
The only complaint I really have is that there's a pretty limited selection of weapons to choose from, though it seems pretty obvious that this is meant to be just a small, quick, fun little game, and as such isn't overflowing with content like that. For the price, I feel like it's totally worth it, especially if you like the "challenging, insta-death" genre.

There is a major gamebreaking control bug in the last boss. It caused me to be unable to complete the game. Due to its severity, I had to change my vote to vote this game down.
PROS
1. Gun and Sword style fighting
It's exactly like playing the beat-them-up games.
2. Quick To Learn
It's super easy to pick up if you've played other beat-them-up games.
3. The Teleporter
Very nice design. I like the way you made it spin before teleportation.
4. Sunlight is Deadly
I like the idea. Not being able to fight in intense solar radiation.
5. Skyguards
Nice idea too.
6. Different Guns / Swords
Nice to know the inventory work differently.
7. The Time Warping
Also cool. Especially when you have to piece together a puzzle to kill a creature. I would have preferred more time powers instead of just rewind.
8. Rocket Launcher
A pity that you are forced to drop it whenever you jump. This is most ridiculous.
9. Executions
Love the way it's quickly executed, even in mid air or mid combat. There is a slight graphics twitch but it's acceptable.
10. Aerial Combat
I love the way you can dash to an enemy and slash him to bits.
11. Creativity
Floating corals? Dying Sun planet? Sky Island? Nice.
CONS
1. Lame Names
Dragonland? Blades of Time?
2. Exact Copy
It's just way too similar to the other beat them up games.
a. Speed Dash
b. Dash Grab
c. Air Dash
d. Range / Melee combo
e. Double Jump
At least, improve on them.
3. Bad Marketing
The team didn't advertise this game well when it was released.
4. Enemies are Carbon Copies
You will see the same enemy in the same Verne model over and over again. The only difference is the top hat. E.g. The mercenaries.
5. No Cities
No rest stops, no shops, just chop chop chop. No additional nuggets of information and lore.
6. Rocket Launcher
It drops when you jump or dash. It's a very silly balance mechanic to prevent you from carrying it over to another location.
7. Graphics
Pretty mediocre. Honestly, there is nothing interesting to look at.
8. Chaos Slasher
That's the Dahaka from Prince of Persia.
9. Floating Coral Grabs
They are the same as grabbing lights in Devil May Cry or Darksiders.
SUGGESTIONS
1. Special Attack Styles
Look at Alice (American McGee) for more details on how to design.
2. More Weapons
I've played the Darksider series and I think more weapons would increase the variety.
3. Flipover / Slide Under
The Prince of Persia series allows you to flip over an opponent. I think this would be a great addition to the movements Ayumi can do. A slide under in between the legs of an enemy would be great too.
4. Flying Gun Combat
Imagine raining rockets while flying or shooting while in the air like Devil May Cry. That would be pretty cool.
5. Co-op Tower Challenge
I think this could be in the next series. Perhaps, Blades of Time is pretty lame so you could make a new series with all the same mechanics.
6. Wall Run / Wall Hop / Wall grab / Wall Combat.
The usual.
7. Stealth Assasinations
Good to have but not compulsory.
8. Swimming
All that water, a bikini and no swimming? What a waste.
9. Complex Puzzles for Big Ticket Stuff
If you have a secret chest or a super boss, finding a hidden location or a complex puzzle would be great. For story progression, simple puzzles and locks.

EDIT 6.11.2017

EDIT:
The game has a great awesome potential but in the present state I can *not* recommend this game.
There are heavy issues (quasi non-existing multiplayer, bad game design aspects which lead that you have to colonize a lot of small planets rather than a few large planets and therefore you lose yourself in mid and end game in too much colonies with too much details instead of having only a few strong planets and clear overview and your head free to think about strategy and decisions instead of doing tons of micromanagmentg - examples for that: growth penalty on large and huge planet and pollution penalty on large and huge planets with big population and strong industry - many small planets with in summary same strong industry suffer not the same pollution penalty, then bugs bugs bugs, a ton of heavy balance issues resp. AI stupidity - even on the hardest difficulty you beat the AI at first attempt, and the developers from NGD studos have abandoned the game, not a word from them and from Wargaming (who has the intellectual property of MoO)  since two months.
One of the big things is the TOTAL FAILURE OF SPACE COMBAT: The AI is not shooting back if you keep your distance:
With a weak ship you can destroy much bigger KI fleets: You use missiles and the AI only uses beam weapons (which have a shorter range).  If you keep your distance you can fire missile after missile after missile while the KI fleet does not fire a single shot back - simply because ther weapons are out of range and they dont build fast ships to quickly bridge the distance.
You dont have to research and build good ships and weapons and shields, armor etc. and build huge armies, if a single weak ship with some lousy missiles is enough to win vs KI even on the hardest difficulty.
Furthermore there is no up-to-date manual and apart from the new stuff in the outdated manual even many of the older things are not explained e.g. that population on small planets growth faster (that is a pretty important thing which you might easily miss to discover if you don't know it), how armor penetration and armor resilience is working (these two terms are in the short tutorial - but missing in the manual), how ground combat is working, etc.
Basically we paid for the game and now it is up to us to fix it. If you did not buy the game I would check back in half a year, because there are many things you can not just mod, in order to improve those things you have to change the code. And btw I don't like the idea that you first have to do your bachelor in MoO and install a ton of mods before you can enjoy your game
Should the developers ever come back and fix the space combat system and the other things then I will write a new review.
BTW: The space combat is in real time though the game is round based. that alone is strange,  but I could forgive it if only it would work with an AI who is able to shoot back in a space battle. There is a guy who writes one game fix mod after another - but the devs do not even apply these fixes in a new version.
